references.note: Theorem (p. 63): f(1/t) = Σ_{n≥1} 1/(t^n − 1) is irrational for every integer |t| > 1; the proof makes long zero blocks in the base-t expansion of Σ d(n)/t^n by a Chinese-remainder choice of consecutive integers with many divisors.
references.title: P. Erdős, On arithmetical properties of Lambert series, J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) 12 (1948), 63–66

references.note: As stated by Kovač–Tao (arXiv:2406.17593, §2.1.2 p. 4): Σ_{n≥1} 1/(t^n + q) is irrational for integer t ≥ 2 and rational q ∉ {0, −t^n}. With t = 2^d, q = −2^(−a): 1/(2^(a+dn) − 1) = 2^(−a)/(t^n + q).
references.title: P. B. Borwein, On the irrationality of Σ 1/(q^n + r), J. Number Theory 37 (1991), 253–259

references.note: Σ_{n≥1} a(n)/(q^n − 1) is irrational for every purely periodic integer sequence a, not identically zero, and every integer |q| > 1. Read in the authors' restatement as Theorem A, RIMS Kôkyûroku 2014 (2017), p. 139 (kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~kyodo/kokyuroku/contents/pdf/2014-14.pdf).
references.title: F. Luca and Y. Tachiya, Irrationality of Lambert series associated with a periodic sequence, Int. J. Number Theory 10 (2014), 623–636, Theorem 1.1

literature_proposed.summary: Known. a = 0 is Erdős 1948 at base 2^d; a ≥ 1 follows from Borwein 1991 after the rescaling in the note (the n = 0 term is rational); all cases also follow from Luca–Tachiya 2014, Theorem 1.1, since an arithmetic progression has a periodic indicator. A Lean proof (Aristotle via agent C, using the periodic case) was submitted on 2026-10-22 as graph PR #873.

justification.text: Real division; the divisor 2^n - 1 is zero only at n = 0, where Lean's junk value makes the term 0, so the sum is the sum over the positive elements, exactly as in the root's acknowledged division.

review.words: Let $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set. Is $$ \sum_{n\in A} \frac{1}{2^n - 1} $$ irrational?

statement.text:
import Mathlib
import Nodes.«variant-886b66da».Context

/-- Erdős 257 for every infinite arithmetic progression `A = {a + d n : n ≥ 0}` (`d ≥ 1`).
Known: for `a = 0` this is Erdős 1948 at base `t = 2^d` (J. Indian Math. Soc. 12, 63–66,
Theorem); for `a ≥ 1`, `1/(2^(a+dn) - 1) = 2^(-a)/(t^n + q)` with `t = 2^d` and `q = -2^(-a)`, so
it follows from P. B. Borwein, *On the irrationality of ∑ 1/(q^n + r)*, J. Number Theory 37
(1991), 253–259: `∑_{n ≥ 1} 1/(t^n + q)` is irrational for every integer `t ≥ 2` and rational
`q ∉ {0, -t^n}` (as stated by Kovač–Tao, arXiv:2406.17593, §2.1.2). The even and the odd
integers are the cases `d = 2`. A `0` in `A` contributes `1/0 = 0` in Lean. -/
theorem Opn.erdos_257_arithmetic_progressions :
    ∀ a d : ℕ, 0 < d →
      Irrational (∑' m : {m : ℕ | ∃ n, m = a + d * n}, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ m.1 - 1)) := by
  sorry
